correctness.rationale: For each of the twelve cube edges, the two associated rhombic edges plus the cube edge contribute exactly one plane crossing in all three allowed low/high sign cases. Affine invariance follows on replacing the normal by the transpose image. Central box sections have four or six vertices; hence rhombic sections have eight or six. For diagonal stretches, each of the 24 rhombic edges has an exactly known pairwise angle, giving the three-arcsine law. A boundary-inclusive Lagrange-multiplier proof establishes unique cubical maximum; the logarithmic Taylor coefficient is reconstructed analytically and checked symbolically. The embedded standalone checker replays exact incidence cases, 12+24 edges, rational-normal evaluations, asymptotic Hessian and independent seeded sampling. Finite tests are not used as universal proof.

value.rationale: The central result is a pointwise nontrivial f-vector complementarity of two distinct convex polyhedra under every common affine transformation, not a numerical restatement. It yields an exact complete all-aspect-ratio law for the natural three-parameter family of triaxial rhombic dodecahedra, a unique cubical extremum and a sharp second-order aspect-ratio stability coefficient. This permits transfer between different section models and serves as a geometry-specific rigidity benchmark; it does not purport to give a new result about the box marginal itself.
